Mapper's Validation Note

14-day window (June 9-23, 2026) produced zero survivors. Broadened to 21-day window (June 2-23, 2026) per protocol. 21-day window added two additional candidates but both failed non-window gates. Dominant failure mode: Gate 4 — most candidates lacked a fetched source explicitly linking the mechanism to AI, ML, or data center workloads in an Alaska-specific sentence. The DOE EDF/Oklo/Eielson candidate appeared promising but collapsed when the Power Magazine Oklo/Eielson article was confirmed dated June 11, 2025 (not 2026) via WebFetch, and the June 23, 2026 DOE EDF announcement covers AP1000 reactors exclusively. The JBER/JITTC-E candidate fell at Gate 4 (TWZ article has no AI language) and Gate 5 (JITTC-E contract already awarded July 2025). This is the tenth consecutive no-target cycle since June 13, 2026. The bar was not lowered. An honest no-target is the correct outcome for this cycle.

The JBER/JITTC-E candidate fell at Gate 4 (TWZ article contains no AI language) and also at Gate 5 (JITTC-E contract was already awarded July 2025, so the claimed binary OTA chokepoint no longer exists).

Persistent pattern: The Kenai LNG Terminal Redevelopment Stack (strong AI-consequence link confirmed via ADN May 5 article) and the Anchorage Title 21 CUP Framework (strong mechanism with clear gate 2–6 coverage) both remain viable but lack an in-window news trigger. Either may become a live target when a qualifying editorial outlet covers a new development — the FERC authorization deadline (July 31, 2026) for the Kenai terminal or a first CUP application filing in Anchorage would both constitute usable triggers.

Recommendation for next cycle: Monitor for (1) any editorial coverage of Harvest Midstream FID or FERC order on the Kenai LNG terminal between June 24 and July 31, 2026; (2) any editorial coverage of the NRC Oklo microreactor licensing progress or a new Eielson power announcement; (3) any independent editorial coverage of the Aleutian Thunder JV beyond the PR Newswire republication.
